title: How to Spot an AI Scam (Contractor Edition)

slides.headline: HOW TO SPOT AN AI SCAM — CONTRACTOR EDITION
slides.body: You've been burned by SEO guys, lead sellers, and coaches. The AI wave has the same sharks. Here's the field guide.

slides.headline: 🚩 1. THEY LEAD WITH "REPLACE YOUR STAFF"
slides.body: Anyone promising to replace your CSR doesn't understand your business. Real automation answers what she can't — the 11pm calls, the overflow — it doesn't fire anyone.

slides.headline: 🚩 2. NO DOLLAR MATH, JUST BUZZWORDS
slides.body: "Leverage AI to transform your business" is a tell. A legit operator talks like this: missed calls run $500–$1,200 each, ~70% of quotes walk without follow-up. If they can't put numbers on YOUR shop, walk.

slides.headline: 🚩 3. ONE TOOL FIXES EVERYTHING
slides.body: It's usually white-labeled software they rent for under $200/mo and resell at $1,500 setup + $500–$1,500/mo. The tool might be fine. The markup and the lock-in aren't.

slides.headline: 🚩 4. LOCKED CONTRACTS, THEIR ACCOUNTS
slides.body: If the phone number, customer list, or review profile lives in THEIR account, you're renting your own business back. 12-month locks on unproven tools = run.

slides.headline: ✅ WHAT LEGIT LOOKS LIKE
slides.body: • Names the problem in YOUR numbers before selling anything • Shows a live demo, not a slide deck • Month-to-month, you own every account • Fine saying "you don't need this yet" • Vendor-neutral — gets paid for results, not kickbacks.

slides.headline: THE SHARKS COUNT ON YOU NOT KNOWING THE QUESTIONS
slides.body: Now you know them. Save this for the next cold pitch that hits your inbox — or send it to a shop owner who's being circled. Got a pitch you're unsure about? Comment or DM it. Free straight answer, no strings.
